subject: Insurance
title: The Chicago Fire of 1871
description: One-minute skill: The Chicago Fire of 1871.

hook.text: The Great Chicago Fire of 1871 destroyed 17,000 buildings. Fifty-eight insurance companies went bankrupt paying claims.

buildup.text: Chicago had boomed with wooden buildings and lax building codes. Insurers underestimated how fast fire would spread.

discovery.text: The companies that survived had spread their risk beyond Chicago. Local-only insurers were wiped out completely.

twist.text: After the fire, Chicago rebuilt with brick and steel. Insurance losses drove building code reforms across America.

climax.text: The Chicago Fire proved that insurance shapes how cities are built. When insurers demand safety, buildings get safer.

punchline.text: 58 insurers bankrupt. Chicago rebuilt safer because insurance demanded it.

quiz.question: How many insurance companies went bankrupt after the Chicago Fire?
